newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close mixed despite high-tech gains.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close mixed despite high-tech gains.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed mixed in active trade on Wednesday, with electronic shares rising on a strong U.S. outlook for semiconductors but financial shares easing on concerns over fundamentals, brokers said.
The weighted index, staying within a narrow range throughout the session, closed 6.17 points or 0.09 percent higher at 6,577.29. Turnover was an active T$51.90 billion.

Electronics gained 1.80 percent on news that the U.S. semiconductor book-to-bill ratio rose to 1.10 in October from 0.98 in September -- indicating a likelihood of strong orders for Taiwan computer chips and other high-tech products.
"The news indicates continuing strength for chipmakers and justifies the high-tech sector's market-leading status," said Allen Huang, an investment manager at National Securities.
While the electronic rally cheered for the overall market, the heavily weighted financials undermined a wider rise.

The sector suffered mild selling on an announcement by Moody's Investors Service late on Monday that it may downgrade the A2 long-term and Prime-1 short-term ratings of Taiwan's "big three" commercial banks -- Chang Hwa, First and Hua Nan -- due to deterioration in their asset quality and relatively weak financial fundamentals. Tuesday was a market holiday.
"The Moody's comment raised investor concerns about the fundamentals of the banking system," Huang said.
While Chang Hwa finished trading even at T$154, First and Hua Nan fell T$2 and T$1, respectively, to T$165 and T$122.50.

Buying was concentrated almost exclusively in electronics shares. First International Computer soared by the daily seven percent limit or T$2.90 to T$45.40. Siliconware and Mitac also finished limit up at T$56 and T$25.70 respectively. Inventec, making its market debut on Wednesday, closed limit up to T$90.50 with only 1,000 shares traded.
"The general feeling is that Inventec's honeymoon bounce will last well into next week," Huang said.
Brokers expected the overall index to remain in a consolidation in the near term.
A 6,550-6,600 trading range was seen for Thursday.
